source.title: A p-adic Simpson correspondence for smooth proper rigid varieties

summary: First checkpoint: source-level extraction of the final published paper, including the coherent/nonreduced Picard argument, finite rigidification, canonical Higgs fields, the exact tensor equivalence and the derived comparison. Reuses named analytic, period-sheaf and Koszul owners. The shared Higgs core is routed to the existing Hitchin owner, not rebuilt privately. Auxiliary-source proof closure, several precise supplier audits and independent review remain open. Two displayed-formula misprints are recorded, not silently repaired. No Lean implementation is claimed.

conventions.base: K is a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p. A rigid space means an analytic adic space locally of topologically finite type over Spa(K,O_K). Global statements assume X smooth and proper; local statements explicitly drop properness.
conventions.sites: nu is Scholze's original, corrected pro-etale-to-etale morphism, with the completed structure sheaf. Do not replace coherent pullback by arbitrary v-pullback. Vector bundles can be compared with the v-site only using the separate comparison theorem.
conventions.coefficients: B is a coherent commutative O_X-algebra, possibly nonreduced and not locally free; script B is nu^*B. From finite rigidification onward B is O_X-torsionfree unless a statement explicitly says otherwise. OmegaTilde=Omega^1_X/K(-1); its k-th exterior power is Omega^k(-k).
conventions.choices: The global functor depends on a smooth B_dR^+/xi^2 lift and a continuous exponential for K. Final objects and maps do not depend on a choice of base point or finite rigidifying set. Naturality requires compatible lifts and compatible exponentials under field embeddings.
conventions.statusMeaning: library means an actual declaration read at the prescribed pin; planned means an existing roadmap interface, not implemented mathematics; missing routes are proposals, not accepted blueprints or completed proofs. Each api list gives intended interfaces, not invented citations to Lean declarations.

baseline.audit: AUDIT-37.result.json was read in the relevant period/adic sections as a search lead. It is NOT independently reviewed: REV-AUDIT-37.md is absent and review issue #872 was open, available and without comments. No reviewed status or exhaustive fresh search of the pinned trees is claimed. See G0.
baseline.additionalOwnerReading: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0-H5 and its proof-accounting sections; PadicHodgeTheory atlas extract; Simpson/Higgs repository searches, including the existing ET.2b Hitchin obligation. The complete global candidate catalogue was not locally available; catalogue and stage validation is delegated to the normal Swarm check.

sourceLedger.version: Publisher version of record, 10 February 2025; Inventiones Mathematicae 240, 261-312
sourceLedger.read: All 52 PDF pages, including references and licence, read through the parsed publisher text. Selected formulas were visually checked against arXiv v3. Publisher screenshot rendering failed; no publisher-image inspection or byte hash is claimed.

Version history and selected sections/visuals: printed pages 5, 10, 23, 26 and 28. Used to verify the rigidification diagram and the two formula slips. No full bytewise or theorem-by-theorem comparison to the publisher version is claimed.

Selected local-correspondence material: Definition 6.2, Lemmas 6.3-6.4, Theorem 6.5 and its construction, Lemmas 6.9-6.11 and the cohomological argument. Integral cocycle descent Proposition 5.5, intertwiner Proposition 5.9 and Appendix A still require complete proof-input extraction.

Selected section 6 definitions and Theorem 6.12 with proof; its Cartesian-diagram input is Fargues Theorem 3.3. This auxiliary version postdates H25 and is explicitly a later source check. The principal-bundle correspondence of section 7 is NOT an input, avoiding a circular dependency.

items.name: Existing Fontaine theta map
items.statement: For the p-adically complete commutative ring hypotheses of the pinned file, reuse WittVector.fontaineTheta from Witt vectors of the pretilt to R. Its Teichmuller evaluation is untilt. Specializing to O_K requires the existing perfectoid-field input; no new theta map is defined by this extraction.
items.locator: Prerequisite to H25 section 2.4; pinned FontaineTheta.lean:160-190
api: Use the existing ring homomorphism and its quotient compatibility
Transport the O_K specialization through the period-ring owner
Retain the pretilt and p-adic completeness hypotheses
testCases: Teichmuller zero maps to zero
Teichmuller one maps to one
Reduction modulo p agrees with the zeroth pretilt coefficient

items.name: Existing theta surjectivity criterion
items.statement: Under the pinned completeness and nonunit-p hypotheses, surjectivity of Frobenius on R/p implies surjectivity of theta. This does not prove that the kernel is principal or that a de Rham period ring is a discrete valuation ring.

items.name: Existing bare B_dR-plus carrier
items.statement: Reuse BDeRhamPlus as the adic completion of the p-inverted Witt ring along the kernel of fontaineThetaInvertP. The pinned file supplies this commutative-ring definition but explicitly leaves extension of theta, principality and DVR results as further work.
items.locator: H25 introduction and section 2.4; pinned BDeRham.lean:61-90
api: Use the existing completion carrier
Compare its ideal and structure map with PadicHodgeTheory R06.1
Obtain xi and filtration only from the proved period package
testCases: The completion ideal is the kernel after p-inversion
The source is the Witt ring of the pretilt, not the tilt itself
No DVR or principal-kernel instance is inferred from the definition

items.name: Original analytic etale and corrected pro-etale sites
items.statement: Import the sites on the existing analytic adic carrier, their ringed morphism nu, inverse/direct images and completed structure sheaf. Preserve Scholze's corrected covering condition; the site used for flat coherent pullback is not replaced by the general v-site.
items.locator: H25 section 2.1, especially the paragraph distinguishing site conventions
api: analyticEtaleSite and originalProetaleSite on one carrier
nu as a ringed-site morphism
Restrictions and completed structure-sheaf comparison
testCases: An etale object gives its ordinary analytic pullback
A toric pro-etale tower uses the corrected covering rule
An arbitrary v-map is not assigned coherent flat pullback

items.name: Coherent analytic modules and finite relative spectra
items.statement: Import coherent sheaves, finite relative spectra, tensor products, locally free modules, proper finiteness and the specified base-change/descent results on analytic adic spaces. A coherent finite algebra need not be locally free, and its relative spectrum retains nilpotent structure.
api: Coherent module/algebra carrier and finite relative Spec
Finite pushforward and proper H0 finiteness
Flat base change and etale descent of vector bundles
testCases: The dual-number algebra remains nonreduced
A finite algebra of varying fibre rank is not declared locally free
Properness is required for finite-dimensional global sections

items.name: Tate-twisted continuous analytic differentials
items.statement: On smooth rigid X/K use the analytic differential sheaf and define OmegaTilde=Omega^1_X/K(-1), with exterior powers Omega^k(-k). Keep the Tate twist in field-change and toric Kummer comparisons instead of choosing roots of unity globally in the public interface.
api: Analytic Kahler differential and Tate-twisted tensor
Exterior powers and pullback differential
Local dlog basis with its Kummer comparison
testCases: A rigid point has zero differentials
A torus has dlog coordinate basis
A field automorphism acts on the Tate factor as well as coefficients

items.name: Early structural period-sheaf package
items.statement: Import structural B_dR-plus, theta, its first infinitesimal quotient and the local Hodge-Tate/Poincare calculations from P8:local-rational. Use the corrected completed integral tensor before p-inversion and theta completion. Do not import the later proper comparison to prove its own local input.
items.locator: H25 section 2.4 and Proposition 2.9 proof; Scholze source convention
api: Structural period sheaf with theta and filtration
First-order quotient and structural map
Local comparison to twisted differentials
testCases: A toric lift uses compatible roots before reduction by xi squared
The p-completed tensor is not replaced by an ordinary tensor
The local package has no CP.3 proper-comparison dependency

items.name: Perfectoid toric torsors and coefficient descent
items.statement: For a toric chart construct the compatible-root tower with group Delta=Z_p(1)^d and its perfectoid limit, completed coefficient rings and descent for finite locally free modules and morphisms. Finite levels are generally not perfectoid; this is a tower theorem, not a limit of already-perfectoid rings argument.
api: Toric tower and continuous Delta action
Completed coefficient ring and integral lattice
Effective descent with morphisms and continuous cochains
testCases: The compatible-root torus is perfectoid
A noncofinal subsystem is not silently the same full tower
Integral descent is not inferred from a rational function equalizer

items.name: Shared Koszul resolution and completion input
items.statement: Import the generic Koszul complex, its differential and regular-sequence resolution theorem, together with the qualified completion/base-change results, from the existing derived-algebra owner. For Sym(L), the augmentation is resolved by the exterior powers of the finite locally free module L. This is not a newly implemented private Simpson complex.
items.locator: H25 Definition 5.4 discussion and proof of Theorem 5.5
api: Koszul complex on a finite sequence
Regular-sequence augmentation quasi-isomorphism
Flat scalar extension and exterior-basis transport
testCases: One polynomial variable resolves its augmentation quotient
A nonregular sequence has extra homology
Changing a basis transports signs and the augmentation

items.name: Derived site cohomology and internal Hom
items.statement: Reuse the ordinary derived sheaf category, Rnu_*, derived global sections, Leray, projection formula in its valid perfect/flat range and Cech-to-derived comparisons on the analytic sites. The object-level comparison in Theorem 5.5 is stronger than equal dimensions or unrelated cohomology-group isomorphisms.
api: Rnu_* and derived internal Hom
Leray edge maps on the actual coefficient sheaves
Cech and acyclic-cover comparison with maps
testCases: The identity site map gives the identity derived functor
A nonacyclic cover does not compute cohomology by degree-zero invariants
Internal RHom is distinguished from global derived Hom

items.name: Representability of etale torsors over an analytic diamond
items.statement: Use the equivalence of etale categories for an analytic adic space and its diamond, including essential surjectivity, to represent the etale torsors arising in the Picard argument. This is not full faithfulness of diamondification on all analytic maps or representability of arbitrary v-sheaves.
items.locator: H25 section 2.7 and proof of Theorem 3.2

items.name: Smooth first-order de Rham lift
items.statement: A lift of smooth rigid X is a smooth space over B_dR^+/xi^2 together with an identification of its reduction with X. Morphisms in the functoriality datum include a compatible morphism of lifts. Existence is a separate theorem, not part of the structure by fiat.
api: Lift with reduction identification
Compatible lifted morphism and composition
Lifting of K-points by smoothness
testCases: The trivial point admits its scalar lift
A lifted map reduces to the stated map of X
A chosen lift is not declared canonical

items.name: Existence of the required first-order lift
items.statement: Every smooth proper rigid X over the stated complete algebraically closed K admits a B_dR^+/xi^2 lift in the sense used by H25. The cited Guo Proposition 7.4.4 must be acquired and its deformation-theoretic hypotheses checked. A canonical deformation of a cohomology complex in CP.3 is not this geometric lift.
items.locator: H25 introduction and Theorem 5.1; Guo, Hodge-Tate decomposition for non-smooth spaces, Proposition 7.4.4

items.name: Pro-etale vector bundle category
items.statement: Use finite locally free modules over the completed structure sheaf on the original pro-etale site, with all module homomorphisms. This category is not restricted to bundles coming from continuous fundamental-group representations or to small bundles globally.
api: Finite locally free module category and pullback
Tensor, dual, direct sum and exact sequences
Comparison of eligible original-pro-etale and v-vector bundles
testCases: Rank zero and the tensor unit are objects
Noninvertible homomorphisms are retained
A bundle outside the representation image is not excluded by definition

items.name: Shared Higgs module and its analytic specialization
items.statement: For a ringed site and finite locally free differential coefficient module, define a locally free E with theta:E to E tensor OmegaTilde satisfying theta wedge theta=0, and morphisms commuting with theta. Build one generic carrier shared with the existing ET.2b Higgs/Hitchin owner; specialize it here to Tate-twisted analytic forms, in any dimension.
items.locator: H25 Definition 1.2; existing ET.2b Higgs obligation
api: Higgs module and commuting morphism
Tensor with sum field, dual field and direct sum
Equivalence with the corresponding symmetric-algebra action
testCases: On a curve the two-form condition is automatic
In dimension two noncommuting coefficient matrices are rejected
The tensor field is theta1 tensor 1 plus 1 tensor theta2

items.name: Relative Picard sheaf for coherent coefficients
items.statement: For coherent O_X-algebra B and script B=nu^*B, define on smooth rigid S the etale sheafification of H1_proet(X times S,script B^units) modulo H1_proet(S,pi_S,*script B^units). This quotient removes bundles pulled from the base. It is not the Picard group of the reduced pro-etale structure sheaf on the finite spectral space.
api: Relative cohomology quotient presheaf
Etale sheafification and base pullback
Functoriality in coherent B and tensor product
testCases: Base-pulled line bundles become zero
B=O_X recovers the relative rank-one problem
B=O_X[epsilon]/epsilon^2 retains infinitesimal units

items.name: Finite-presentation integral model of coherent coefficients
items.statement: A coherent analytic module B admits a finitely presented O_X^+-model B0 with B0[1/p]=B; if B is an algebra, choose an algebra model. Use formal-model and flattening inputs at their actual hypotheses. B^+=B0/B0[p-infinity] is allowed to be noncoherent.
items.proof: Use a formal model and finite presentations locally, extend after admissible modifications, and glue; preserve the distinction between the finitely presented model and its torsionfree image.

items.name: Descent of additive coefficient quotients
items.statement: For the integral model of Lemma 2.7, script B/p^k script B^+ is the inverse-image sheaf of B/p^k B^+, and its derived pushforward is concentrated in degree zero. The comparison is used before applying small exponentials, with the original pro-etale site convention.

items.name: Descent of unit quotients
items.statement: The quotient script B^units/(1+p script B^+) descends from the etale unit quotient, with the p=2 small subgroup adjusted as in Lemma 2.8. The result concerns a quotient of unit sheaves; it does not identify all units with additive sections.

items.name: Convergent small exponential for coherent coefficients
items.statement: Construct the sheaf exponential and logarithm between the sufficiently small additive lattice and multiplicative units. Use p B^+ for odd p and 4 B^+ for p=2, or uniformly 2p B^+. Extend to script B to script B^units[1/p] by p-divisibility. This is separate from a chosen global exponential on K-points.
api: Small exp/log with convergence bounds
Additive-to-multiplicative group law
Rationalized sheaf exponential and restriction compatibility
testCases: At p=2 the terms for exp(2) fail the uniform convergence test
Exp(4x) is inside the uniform p=2 lattice
Nilpotent coefficients recover finite exp/log polynomials

items.name: Exactness of coherent pullback on the original pro-etale site
items.statement: For coherent B on smooth X, Lnu^*B is represented by nu^*B. Prove this by local finite free resolutions and the flatness/completion argument on suitable toric towers; arbitrary maps on the v-site do not provide this conclusion.
items.proof: Shrink to finite free resolutions, control integral torsion uniformly, and pass through the completed toric coefficient algebra before using the projection formula.

items.name: Coherent additive Hodge-Tate direct images
items.statement: For coherent B on smooth X and n at least zero, R^n nu_*(nu^*B) is naturally B tensor OmegaTilde^n. The completed structure-sheaf calculation is an imported local period theorem; the extension to possibly nonflat coherent B uses flat-coherent-pullback.

items.name: Multiplicative Hodge-Tate direct images
items.statement: For a coherent commutative algebra B, nu_*(script B^units)=B^units and, for n at least one, R^n nu_*(script B^units) is naturally B tensor OmegaTilde^n. The n=0 term stays multiplicative and is not B itself.
items.proof: Compare the small additive and multiplicative lattices by exp/log, then use the descended quotient sheaves and the additive calculation.

items.name: Left-exact Hodge-Tate edge sequences
items.statement: Leray gives additive and multiplicative left-exact sequences with H1_et(X,B) or H1_et(X,B^units), pro-etale H1, and H0(X,B tensor OmegaTilde). Do not assert right-surjectivity here: properness, the lift and the relative Picard argument supply the later splitting/surjectivity.

items.name: Higgs-Tate torsor associated to the lift
items.statement: Define the sheaf of lifts of the structural map from the chosen first-order lift to the first-order structural period sheaf. Differences of lifts identify it as a torsor under nu^*OmegaTilde-dual. Construct the pushout comparison for compatible morphisms of lifted spaces.
api: Lift-of-structure-map sheaf
Translation action and torsor property
Pullback/pushout along a compatible lifted morphism
testCases: Two lifts differ by a derivation
The point case has the trivial zero-dimensional torsor
Composition of lifted maps agrees with iterated pushout

items.name: Coefficient pushout of the Higgs-Tate torsor
items.statement: For theta in H0(X,B tensor OmegaTilde), dualize to OmegaTilde-dual to B and push out the Higgs-Tate torsor to an additive script B-torsor. Construct additivity, B-functoriality and the universal family over the vector group A_B.
api: Pushout torsor along theta
Additive and coefficient-change isomorphisms
Universal torsor over X times A_B
testCases: Theta zero gives the trivial torsor
Theta1+theta2 gives the contracted sum
Nilpotent-valued theta is not replaced by its reduction

items.name: Toric formula and normalization of the lift torsor
items.statement: On a compatible toric lift the Higgs-Tate torsor is described by the Kummer coordinate cocycle sum_i c_i(gamma) partial_i. Match the chosen compatible roots, Teichmuller lifts modulo xi squared, dlog coordinates and the Tate twist, proving HT of the coefficient pushout is its specified theta.
items.locator: H25 Lemma 2.16 and proof of Proposition 2.15

items.name: Lift-dependent additive Hodge-Tate splitting
items.statement: The coefficient pushout gives a K-linear map H0(X,B tensor OmegaTilde) to H1_proet(X,script B) that splits the Hodge-Tate edge map. It is natural in B and compatible lifted maps. Its dependence on the chosen lift is retained.

items.name: Relative Hodge-Tate logarithm
items.statement: Construct HTlog from the relative Picard sheaf to the rigid vector group A_B=H0(X,B tensor OmegaTilde) tensor G_a. In a product with a smooth parameter S, quotienting by base cohomology removes the Omega_S contribution; retain this relative normalization.
api: Vector group A_B with coefficient base change
Relative HTlog on Picard classes
Compatibility with tensor, inverse and restriction
testCases: A base-pulled class has relative HTlog zero
Tensor products add their HTlog sections
The dual line has the negative HTlog section

items.name: Analytic splitting on an open lattice
items.statement: HTlog admits an analytic section on a sufficiently small open subgroup of A_B. Choose an integral cohomology lattice spanning H1 after inverting p, lift a finite free lattice through it, use the additive splitting and shrink into the small exponential domain. This does not produce an analytic global exponential on A_B.

items.name: Proper rigid base change for constant finite torsion
items.statement: For proper rigid Z over the algebraically closed K and a smooth rigid parameter S, the higher direct image of Z/n along Z times S to S is the constant cohomology sheaf of Z, in the range of H25 Proposition 2.18. Z can be singular and n can have a p-factor. The older prime-to-residue-characteristic invariance theorem alone is insufficient.
items.locator: H25 Proposition 2.18; Bhatt-Hansen, Theorem 3.15, cited proof input

items.name: Connected parameters kill locally constant quotient obstructions
items.statement: A map from a connected rigid space to a sheaf quotient of locally constant sheaves is constant in the situation of Lemma 2.21. Etale-local lifts and openness of their images are needed; checking only a set-theoretic function on K-points does not establish the sheaf statement.

items.name: Exact multiplicative relative Hodge-Tate sequence
items.statement: For smooth proper X and coherent algebra B, there is a natural short exact sequence of etale sheaves 0 to Pic(X') to Pic_scriptB,proet to A_B to 0, where X'=Spec_X B retains nilpotents. In particular HTlog is sheaf-surjective, not merely surjective after an unverified choice on K-points.
items.proof: Use finite-pushforward and Kummer comparisons, proper torsion base change, the open splitting and the constant-quotient lemma to eliminate the H2 obstruction over the connected vector group.

items.name: Conditional representability of the full relative Picard sheaf
items.statement: If the ordinary analytic Picard sheaf of X'=Spec_X B is represented by a rigid group, then the pro-etale Picard sheaf is represented by a rigid group. The ordinary representability assumption is essential to this statement; it is removed only for the smaller group constructed in section 3.1.
items.proof: Build open subsets above p-power dilations of the splitting lattice and represent their etale torsor transitions by the analytic-diamond etale comparison.

items.name: Lie algebra of the Picard extension
items.statement: In the representable case the Lie sequence is 0 to H1_et(X,B) to H1_proet(X,script B) to H0(X,B tensor OmegaTilde) to 0. Prove the tangent identification on the smooth test category through small additive groups; the dual-number test object is not in that category.

items.name: Finite etaleness of multiplication by p on the Picard identity component
items.statement: When the full Picard sheaf is representable, its identity component has finite etale multiplication-by-p map as specified in Theorem 2.4(5). The finite kernel comes from the proper Kummer calculation, and the obstruction on the connected component vanishes. Do not infer finiteness merely from a Lie algebra computation.

items.name: Algebraizable spectral-cover specialization
items.statement: If X and its coherent algebra arise from proper algebraic data, GAGA and the appropriate algebraic Picard representability theorem give the ordinary Picard hypothesis used above, including nonreduced finite covers. The source-specific Picard hypotheses and precise general owner still need matching; this is not supplied by a Jacobian theorem for smooth curves alone.

items.name: Universal exponential class after p-inversion
items.statement: Apply the rationalized sheaf exponential to the universal additive Higgs-Tate torsor to obtain e_lift:A_B to Pic_scriptB,proet[1/p], splitting HTlog after p-inversion. This constructs a section of sheaves with p inverted, not yet a preferred actual invertible script B-module.
api: Universal rationalized multiplicative torsor
Section of the rationalized HTlog
Naturality in B and the lift
testCases: The zero section maps to the trivial class
Multiplication by p commutes with the construction
A rationalized class is not silently promoted to a chosen line bundle

items.name: Always representable reduction of the Picard group
items.statement: Define P_lift,B as the equalizer of the canonical p-inversion map and e_lift composed with HTlog. It fits into 0 to Pic(X')[p-infinity] to P_lift,B to A_B to 0 and is represented by a rigid group even when the full ordinary Picard functor is not known representable.
api: Equalizer sheaf and map to Pic_scriptB
Kernel identification with p-primary torsion
Rigid representability and Lie(P)=A_B(K)
testCases: The zero fibre is the p-primary Picard subgroup
No representability of all Pic(X') is assumed
The universal section agrees after p-inversion

items.name: p-divisibility and surjectivity on the reduced Picard identity component
items.statement: The identity component P_lift,B^0 is p-divisible and still maps surjectively to A_B. Prove representability by etale torsors with constant torsion kernel, then use the component/cokernel diagram and connectedness to show multiplication by p is surjective on that component.

items.name: Units of a connected finite algebra, retaining nilpotents
items.statement: If A is a finite connected algebra over algebraically closed characteristic-zero K and N is its nilradical, then for every K-algebra R, (A tensor R)^units is naturally isomorphic as a group to (N tensor R,+) times R^units. Use the unique augmentation A to K and finite nilpotent exp/log, not reduction of A.

items.name: Split unit-group embeddings for finite algebras
items.statement: For an injection A to A' of finite K-algebras, their unit sheaves are represented by products of additive and multiplicative rigid groups; the induced unit map is split injective and its cokernel is again such a product. Include the base-site cohomology splitting used by Proposition 3.7. The splitting need not be canonical.

items.name: Finite evaluation detects global sections of a torsionfree coherent algebra
items.statement: For coherent O_X-torsionfree B on smooth proper X, there are finitely many K-points for which H0(X,B) to the product of B-fibres is injective. Proper finiteness and torsionfreeness are used. A single point need not work, and fibre evaluations need not detect torsion supported on an infinitesimal thickening.

items.name: Rigidifying multiset and lifted rigidifying set
items.statement: A finite multiset M of K-points is B-rigidifying when its evaluation map is injective. A finite set of lifted points is rigidifying when its reduction, counted with multiplicities, is rigidifying. Distinct lifted points can have the same reduction, so replacing the reduction multiset by a set loses data.
api: Evaluation at an indexed finite multiset
Rigidifying predicate and monotonicity under enlargement
Reduction of a finite lifted set with multiplicities
testCases: Repeated reduced points retain separate chosen lifts
Degree-d polynomial sections are detected by d+1 distinct evaluations
One evaluation does not detect all positive-degree sections

items.name: Relative Picard quotient already satisfies etale descent
items.statement: For torsionfree coherent B the unsheafified relative cohomology quotient in Definition 2.2 agrees with the sheafified Picard functor on smooth rigid parameters. Rigidifying evaluations split the base H2 map in the five-term Leray sequence. This gives actual relative line representatives, not just local classes.

items.name: The group measuring choices of finite rigidification
items.statement: Define Q_M as the quotient of the product of fibre-unit sheaves at M by the unit sheaf of H0(X,B). It is a sheaf represented by G_a^r times G_m^s, using the injective evaluation and split finite-algebra unit theorem. Its Lie algebra is the corresponding quotient of additive fibres by H0(X,B).
api: Fibre-unit quotient Q_M
Representability and additive Lie quotient
Maps under enlargement of M
testCases: For connected X, B=O_X and one point, Q_M is trivial
Extra points add rigidification parameters
Nilpotent fibre units contribute additive factors

items.name: Invertible coherent-coefficient module with finite rigidification
items.statement: An M-rigidified invertible script B-module is a line module together with a trivialization on each indexed fibre over M. Morphisms preserve each trivialization; tensor, inverse and the trivial object carry induced rigidifications. Do not quotient by isomorphism before defining this groupoid and its morphisms.
api: Rigidified line objects and compatible isomorphisms
Tensor, inverse and trivial rigidified object
Forgetting or enlarging rigidification data
testCases: A scalar automorphism preserving all detecting fibres is identity
Tensor fibre trivializations multiply
Two incompatible trivializations need not admit a compatible isomorphism

items.name: Uniqueness of compatible rigidified isomorphisms
items.statement: Between two M-rigidified invertible script B-modules there is at most one compatible isomorphism, because the ratio of two isomorphisms is a global unit detected by M. This proves uniqueness, not existence, and is the mechanism that turns isomorphism classes into coherent canonical choices.

items.name: Rigidified Picard sheaf and reduced subgroup
items.statement: Define Pic_scriptB^M as isomorphism classes of M-rigidified lines and P_lift,B^M as its pullback over P_lift,B. Prove sheaf descent using uniqueness of compatible isomorphisms, which forces the cocycle condition. These are rigidified moduli problems, not a free choice of representatives of the unrigidified Picard group.
api: Rigidified Picard functor
Pullback defining P^M
Descent, forgetful and enlargement maps
testCases: Compatible local rigidified objects descend uniquely
Noncompatible fibre trivializations fail descent
Forgetting M recovers the unrigidified isomorphism class

items.name: Rigidified reduced Picard group is represented
items.statement: There are exact sequences 0 to Q_M to Pic^M to Pic to 0 and 0 to Q_M to P^M to P to 0 in the respective etale/analytic topology of Theorem 3.14. The latter is analytically locally split and always represented by a rigid group. Its identity component admits the required surjective p-map.

items.name: Linearized rigidified torsors
items.statement: Define LP^M by additive script B-torsors with the specified fibre trivializations, modulo global additive translations. It is a vector group in an exact sequence 0 to LQ_M to LP^M to A_B to 0, and is identified with Lie(P^M) by the small-exponential argument.
api: Additively rigidified torsor and quotient
Vector-group exact sequence
Comparison with the tangent/Lie object of P^M
testCases: Zero torsor with zero fibre sections gives zero
Changing all sections by one global section is quotiented out
The Lie quotient uses additive fibres, not their units

items.name: Lie splitting determined by lifted points
items.statement: Each lifted point trivializes the Higgs-Tate torsor on the corresponding fibre. For a lifted rigidifying set these trivializations give a section s_lift,M:A_B to LP^M of the linearized exact sequence, compatible with coefficient maps and forgetting lifted points.
api: Fibre section induced by a chosen lifted point
Section of the linear rigidification extension
Functoriality for common enlargements of lifted sets
testCases: Two different lifts at one reduced point are kept distinct
The zero coefficient section gets the zero rigidification
Forgetting an extra lifted point commutes with the splitting

items.name: Choice of global continuous scalar exponential
items.statement: An exponential for K is a homomorphism Exp:(K,+) to 1+m_K splitting log and agreeing with the convergent exponential on p^alpha m_K, where alpha=1/(p-1) for odd p and alpha=2 for p=2. It is continuous but is not asserted to be a global analytic morphism of rigid groups.
api: Exp with log-section and small-series agreement
Continuity from the small-domain agreement
Compatibility condition for a field embedding
testCases: Log(Exp(x))=x for every x
No global rigid analytic G_a-to-open-disc section is inferred

items.name: Existence of a scalar exponential under the stated field hypothesis
items.statement: For complete algebraically closed K as above a scalar exponential exists. Its existence uses the divisibility/Kummer property in HWZ Lemma 6.2; the choice is retained in the global Simpson datum. No functorial canonical choice for all field embeddings is claimed.

items.name: Topological p-torsion and rigid logarithm
items.statement: For a commutative rigid group G define its topological p-torsion subgroup Ghat=Hom(Z_p,G), with its open rigid realization and logarithm. Under the p-divisibility hypotheses, 0 to G[p-infinity] to Ghat to Lie(G) tensor G_a to 0 is exact. Distinguish topological p-torsion from finite p-primary torsion and from all topological torsion.
api: Ghat and evaluation at 1
Logarithm with kernel G[p-infinity]
Naturality under homomorphisms and identity components
testCases: A nontorsion element approaching 1 under p-powers can lie in Ghat
Prime-to-p torsion is not added indiscriminately
The log kernel and its image are proved separately

items.name: Analytic p-divisible group classification input to exponentiation
items.statement: The analytic p-divisible group associated to the identity component of Ghat has the functorial Cartesian description with its Lie algebra and Tate-module dual used in HWZ Theorem 6.12. Fargues Theorem 3.3 supplies this nontrivial classification; its full statement, proof and precise owner are not yet extracted here.
items.locator: HWZ Theorem 6.12 proof; Fargues, Groupes analytiques rigides p-divisibles, Theorem 3.3

items.name: Functorial Lie exponential induced by the scalar choice
items.statement: For a commutative rigid G whose p-map is surjective on K-points, Exp_K induces a continuous homomorphism Exp_G:Lie(G) to Ghat(K) splitting log_G, naturally in G. Use the Cartesian analytic-p-divisible classification, not an assumed analytic section of every logarithm sequence.
items.proof: Apply Exp_K to the Hom-of-Tate-module coordinate in Fargues's Cartesian square and pull the section back; naturality follows from that of the square.

items.name: Symmetric-algebra action and tautological coefficient section
items.statement: For T_X=Sym(OmegaTilde-dual) and a coherent T_X-algebra B, dualize the generating map OmegaTilde-dual to B to obtain tau_B in H0(X,B tensor OmegaTilde). This is the shared symmetric-algebra/Higgs interface, independent of p-adic exponentiation.
api: Symmetric algebra acting through commuting generators
Tautological section tau_B
Compatibility with algebra maps and sums of actions
testCases: The augmentation action gives tau=0
A nilpotent matrix gives a nonzero nilpotent section
A tensor action gives the sum of the two transported sections

items.name: Canonical exponential invertible module
items.statement: For coherent O_X-torsionfree T_X-algebra B, exponentiate s_lift,M(tau_B) in the rigidified Picard identity component, choose its unique rigidified object, and compare common enlargements of lifted rigidifying sets. This produces an invertible script B-module L_B with HTlog(L_B)=tau_B, canonical up to coherent unique rigidified identifications rather than only an isomorphism class.
api: L_B with its Picard class and HTlog
Canonical rigidifications at lifted points
Choice comparison through unions of lifted sets
testCases: The augmentation algebra yields the unit line
Two rigidifying sets agree after their common enlargement
Reducing B before exponentiation is not allowed

items.name: Functorial coefficient change for the canonical line
items.statement: For a morphism B to B' of coherent torsionfree T_X-algebras, construct L_B tensor_scriptB scriptB' isomorphic to L_B', and prove identity and composition compatibilities using common rigidifications and functorial Lie exponentiation.

items.name: Lifted geometric and scalar naturality of the canonical line
items.statement: Under a compatible morphism of smooth proper lifted spaces and compatible scalar exponentials, the canonical line pulls back to the canonical line for the torsionfree quotient of the pulled-back spectral algebra. Preserve the quotient and the compatibility of the differential/Tate-twist maps.

items.name: Tensor identity for canonical exponential lines
items.statement: For the coefficient tensor construction of Theorem 3.22(4), the canonical line of the torsionfree tensor algebra with sum Higgs section identifies with the tensor product of the transported canonical lines, compatibly with association. The exact O_X-algebra versus T_X-algebra scope at the invocation in Theorem 5.1 is a separate hypothesis check recorded in G6; no unverified strengthening is hidden here.
items.locator: H25 Theorem 3.22(4) and Theorem 5.1 tensor proof

items.name: Actual spectral image algebra of a Higgs field
items.statement: Define B_theta as the image of T_X to End(E), not as an arbitrarily selected characteristic-polynomial cover. It is a coherent commutative O_X-torsionfree algebra and can have nilpotents or fail to be locally free. Its tautological section acts as theta.
api: Image algebra and faithful action on E
Coherence and torsionfreeness on smooth X
Comparison between tau_B and theta
testCases: Two size-two nilpotent blocks have image algebra K[t]/t^2, not K[t]/t^4
Zero Higgs field has scalar image
A nonreduced image is not replaced by its reduced spectral space

items.name: Independence of a larger coefficient algebra
items.statement: Replacing B_theta by a larger coherent torsionfree T_X-algebra mapping to it gives the same twisted vector bundle after the canonical line base-change identification. This permits common algebras for direct sums and tensors without asserting that every vector-bundle morphism directly gives a map between its two minimal spectral algebras.
items.locator: H25 Remark 4.2 and proof of Theorem 5.1

items.name: Chart-dependent Kummer-to-differential map
items.statement: For a toric chart f:U to T^d and its Delta torsor, construct rho_f:H0(U,OmegaTilde) to Hom_cont(Delta,O(U)) and its coherent B-coefficient version. Keep the chart, integral lattice and Tate twist as inputs; change of chart is addressed by the later canonical-field theorem, not by definition.
api: Toric chart and Kummer basis
rho_f and rho_f,B
Integral smallness lattice and compatible chart morphisms
testCases: A dlog coordinate gives its Kummer character
Restriction along a compatible chart map commutes
Different charts are not definitionally assigned equal local Simpson functors

items.name: Source-qualified small bundles and Higgs fields
items.statement: Fix the toric chart and an integral good-reduction subgroup/lattice. Smallness means admitting the reduction required by the cocycle descent constant in H22 Proposition 5.5, with the compatible integral bound on theta. The bound can depend on the chart/space and is not the unqualified condition norm(theta)<1.
api: Small pro-etale bundle with witnessed reduction
Small Higgs module with bounded coefficients
Preservation only under eligible chart changes and tower levels
testCases: The zero field with trivial integral bundle is small
A general pullback is not automatically declared small
Moving up the toric tower preserves the applicable descent constant

items.name: Exact local Simpson equivalence on small objects
items.statement: For a fixed toric chart, small pro-etale vector bundles and small Higgs bundles form exactly equivalent categories, including noninvertible morphisms. The inverse descends the semilinear action exp(rho_f(theta)). Essential surjectivity and full faithfulness require the integral cocycle and intertwiner arguments, not just the displayed exponential formula.

items.name: Etale-local reduction to the small correspondence
items.statement: Every pro-etale vector bundle becomes small after an etale cover in the setting used by H25. Obtain a reduction, trivialize on a toric perfectoid tower, then pass to an open subgroup of Delta while retaining the correct descent constant. This does not make the original bundle globally small.

items.name: Local line module with prescribed Hodge-Tate logarithm
items.statement: Etale-locally, an invertible script B-module of HTlog tau is represented on a toric cover by gamma(a tensor x)=gamma(a) tensor (exp(rho_f,B(tau)(gamma)) times x), after shrinking Delta into the 2p B^+ domain. The factor x is essential and corrects E1.
api: Continuous multiplicative cocycle with convergence witness
Semilinear action including multiplication on x
Descent line and HTlog computation
testCases: The action sends zero to zero
The identity of Delta acts as identity
The cocycle law gives the group action composition law

items.name: Local Simpson inverse as coherent-algebra twisting
items.statement: For a small Higgs bundle with spectral algebra B, the local Simpson inverse is nu^*E tensor_scriptB L_tau,f. The same description holds etale-locally for arbitrary Higgs bundles after the smallness reduction. Coefficient tensoring is over B, not necessarily over O_X alone.

items.name: Coherence of pushed-forward endomorphisms
items.statement: For every pro-etale vector bundle V on smooth X, nu_*End(V) is coherent. Use the local small correspondence and its treatment of all endomorphisms. This does not assert that nu_*V itself is a vector bundle.

items.name: Choice-free Higgs field on every pro-etale vector bundle
items.statement: Construct theta_V:V to V tensor nu^*OmegaTilde, independently of toric charts, lifts and Exp. Locally use the small correspondence; compare different charts through a common coherent spectral algebra and local lines with equal HTlog. Functoriality with respect to all endomorphisms removes the remaining conjugation ambiguity.
api: theta_V on the original pro-etale bundle
Comparison with every local small-correspondence field
Chart-independent gluing on overlaps
testCases: The completed structure sheaf has zero field
All endomorphisms commute with theta_V
Two chart constructions agree as fields, not only up to an unspecified conjugation

items.name: Naturality of the canonical field
items.statement: Every pro-etale vector-bundle homomorphism commutes with the canonical fields, and their construction is compatible with the pullbacks in Theorem 4.8. In particular nonisomorphisms and endomorphisms enter the argument; an equivalence of isomorphism groupoids alone is not sufficient.

items.name: Integrability of the canonical field
items.statement: The canonical field satisfies theta_V wedge theta_V=0. Verify this in each local small model where the coefficient operators commute, then descend equality. The condition is substantive in dimension at least two.

items.name: Canonical field on a twisted analytic Higgs bundle
items.statement: If L is an invertible script B-module with HTlog tau_B, then on nu^*E tensor_scriptB L the canonical field equals the transported analytic Higgs field. This comparison, including the toric case, is what makes global twisting invertible; equality of underlying bundles alone would not suffice.

items.name: Spectral image algebra of a pro-etale bundle
items.statement: Use the canonical field to define B_V as the image of T_X to nu_*End(V), with tautological tau_V. Coherence follows from Corollary 4.5 and torsionfreeness from its action. Its definition does not depend on choosing a local analytic representative of V.
api: Image algebra B_V and action on V
Coherence/torsionfreeness and tau_V
Common image for direct sums and comparison after twisting
testCases: Zero canonical field has scalar spectral image
A local nilpotent field retains its nilpotent image
Changing a local trivialization conjugates the action but not the intrinsic image object

items.name: Untwisting descends to an analytic Higgs bundle
items.statement: For B=B_V and any L with HTlog tau_V, V tensor_scriptB L^{-1} is the pullback of an analytic vector bundle E with a descended Higgs field. Compare with the local exponential line; their ratio has HTlog zero by addition of the logarithm of the inverse, correcting E2. Then apply the etale kernel description and analytic descent.

items.name: Global Simpson functors on objects
items.statement: Define S(V)=nu_*((V,theta_V) tensor_scriptB_V L_BV^{-1}) and T(E,theta)=nu^*E tensor_scriptB_theta L_Btheta. Use untwisting descent to prove S(V) lies in the analytic Higgs category; these expressions are not merely formal tensor symbols on unrelated coefficient carriers.
api: S and T on objects with their coefficient maps
Canonical field and descended analytic field comparisons
Dependence on the specified lift and Exp
testCases: The tensor unit maps to the zero-field unit
The functor accepts globally nonsmall objects
The inverse uses the actual image algebra, not a chosen reduced cover

items.name: Global Simpson maps on all homomorphisms
items.statement: For a homomorphism V to W, use the common spectral algebra of V direct-sum W. Naturality of the canonical field applied to the endomorphism (v,w) to (v,w+phi(v)) proves the needed B-linearity. Canonical line base change then defines S(phi). Use triple direct sums to prove composition.
api: S on morphisms through a common coefficient algebra
Identity and composition proofs
Independence of the common larger algebra
testCases: The zero homomorphism remains zero
A noninvertible inclusion is handled
Two composable maps agree with the triple-direct-sum construction

items.name: Unit and counit of the global equivalence
items.statement: The two functors are quasi-inverse with natural unit and counit. Identify the two spectral images using the canonical-field comparison after twisting, then cancel the canonical line and its inverse. Prove the morphism compatibilities, not just objectwise existence of isomorphisms.

items.name: Exact tensor structure of the global correspondence
items.statement: The global equivalence is exact and tensor. Exactness is checked in compatible local small models. Tensor compatibility uses the torsionfree quotient of B1 tensor_OX B2 with the sum field, the canonical line tensor identity, and comparison with the image algebra on E1 tensor E2. Unit and associativity constraints must be coherent; see G6 for the tensor-input scope check.

items.name: Naturality in compatible lifted geometric data
items.statement: The equivalence is natural for the compatible lifted maps and scalar exponentials specified in Theorem 5.1. The Tate twist and torsionfree pulled-back spectral algebra remain part of the comparison. No unqualified canonical equivalence independent of lift and Exp is asserted.

items.name: A connected family joining the bundle to its analytic untwist
items.statement: If S(V)=(E,theta), there is a connected smooth rigid parameter space with two points and a pro-etale vector bundle on X times that space whose fibres are nu^*E and V. Use the reduced Picard identity component and the existence of a relative line representative from Proposition 3.7.

items.name: Higgs complex and Dolbeault hypercohomology
items.statement: For an integrable Higgs bundle define the complex E to E tensor OmegaTilde to E tensor OmegaTilde^2 and so on, with differential theta wedge, and define its derived global sections. Integrability gives differential squared zero. Preserve cohomological degrees, wedge signs and Tate twists.
api: Higgs cochain complex with d squared zero
Functorial map from a Higgs morphism
Dolbeault hypercohomology in the existing derived category
testCases: Zero Higgs field has zero differentials
Two noncommuting matrices fail the complex condition
Degree k carries twist minus k

items.name: Higgs complex as derived Hom from the augmentation
items.statement: Use the shared Koszul resolution of O_X over T_X=Sym(OmegaTilde-dual) to identify the Higgs complex with internal RHom_T_X(O_X,E). Applying derived global sections gives the global Ext/Dolbeault statement. Do not conflate the sheaf-valued and global derived Hom objects.

items.name: Qualified flatness of the spectral-adic completion
items.statement: Use the local noetherian, finitely generated-ideal completion theorem to prove flatness of T_X to its J-adic completion in the coherent spectral setting. General completion is not flat without hypotheses, and ordinary completion is not substituted for a derived completion over arbitrary rings.

items.name: Completion along the spectral ideal, not initially the augmentation
items.statement: Let J be the kernel of T_X to End(E), and form the inverse limit of T_X/J^n. This is the spectral-adic completion. Enlarge the coefficient algebra, equivalently shrink J, when needed so J is contained in the augmentation ideal; do not confuse the original spectral ideal with the zero-section ideal.
api: Spectral ideal J and coherent thickened algebras B_n
Qualified completion and E-action
Comparison after adjoining the zero-section component
testCases: A nonzero scalar Higgs value has spectral ideal different from augmentation
Adjoining the zero action makes the new ideal lie in augmentation
The completed action on E still factors through B_1

items.name: Compatible lines on spectral thickenings
items.statement: For B_n=T_X/J^n, use the unrigidified exponential class to choose lines L_n and compatible reductions, starting with L_B. B_n need not be O_X-torsionfree, so Theorem 3.22 cannot be applied directly. Finite-dimensional global Hom spaces give the required Mittag-Leffler control for comparisons of systems; the inverse-limit sheaf and automorphism compatibility require the checks in G7.
api: Exponential isomorphism classes for all coherent B_n
Compatible reductions L_(n+1) to L_n
Limit invertible module and comparison of chosen systems
testCases: A torsion-containing thickening is not fed to the torsionfree rigidification theorem
Reduction of the limit gives L_B
Changing transition representatives must not change the induced comparison map

items.name: Natural global derived comparison morphism
items.statement: Apply tensoring by the completed line to the flatly base-changed Koszul resolution, identify the twisted E with V and the augmentation twist with the unit, and construct C_Higgs(E,theta) to Rnu_*V. Prove independence of compatible thickened-line choices and naturality through common coefficient algebras before checking it locally.
api: Comparison morphism in D(X_et)
Naturality in E and coefficient enlargement
Independence of line-system and transition choices
testCases: The zero-field unit gives the standard Hodge-Tate comparison
Two coefficient enlargements give the same derived morphism
Automorphisms of an auxiliary line cannot introduce an untracked scalar in the result

items.name: Convergent local algebra lifting the canonical line
items.statement: On a toric small chart use the chart integral differential lattice and the convergent algebra O_U<p^{-alpha} partial_1,...,p^{-alpha} partial_d>. Smallness extends the action on E to this algebra. The cocycle gamma_i to exp(partial_i) defines a line over it, allowing explicit comparison with spectral completion and the Koszul complex.
api: Scaled Tate algebra and maps into completion diagrams
Extension of the small E-action
Exponential Delta-cocycle and descended line
testCases: The scale makes each exponential converge
Outside the smallness bound the extension is not assumed
The zero generator acts by the identity in the cocycle

items.name: Continuous toric cohomology computed by a Koszul complex
items.statement: For the eligible continuous Delta=Z_p^d module and topology, continuous cohomology is computed by the Koszul operators gamma_i-1. Preserve the integral modulo-p^k and inverse-limit hypotheses in H22 Appendix A. A Koszul calculation for a discrete group ring alone is not the completed continuous theorem.
items.locator: H25 Lemma 5.7; H22 Lemma A.5 and Lemma 6.11

items.name: Uniform torsion control in toric coefficient extension
items.statement: For a sufficiently small integral representation rho of Delta and M=(R^+)^n or its quotient modulo p^k, the map of continuous cohomology under R^+ to R_infinity^+ has kernel and cokernel killed by one p-power independent of k. In degree zero for the unquotiented module it is an isomorphism. Inverting p then supplies the rational comparison.
items.locator: H22 Lemma 6.9 and proof; H25 Lemma 5.7 input
items.proof: Decompose into fractional toric monomials, control nonzero character terms by a root-of-unity factor times a unit, reduce to Z_p via continuous cohomology and retain a uniform annihilator before the limit.

items.name: The local comparison is a quasi-isomorphism
items.statement: The local derived comparison map identifies, after the explicit toric construction, with the comparison of Koszul operators gamma_i-1 and log(gamma_i). The quotient power series is an invertible commuting operator in the small range. Verify the exterior-degree chain map and that it is the restriction of the globally constructed map, not merely an unrelated local isomorphism.

items.name: Derived sheaf and global cohomological Simpson comparison
items.statement: For V and its associated (E,theta), the constructed map gives a natural isomorphism Rnu_*V with C_Higgs(E,theta) in D(X_et); hence RGamma_proet(X,V) is naturally isomorphic to Dolbeault hypercohomology. The source does not prove an extension of the correspondence to all perfect complexes in this paper.

items.name: Continuous representations embed, but do not exhaust the source category
items.statement: For connected smooth proper X with a base point, descent from the universal profinite-etale cover gives a fully faithful functor from finite-dimensional continuous K-representations of pi_1(X) to pro-etale vector bundles, and composing with S gives an exact tensor embedding into Higgs bundles. The image characterization is not supplied by the main equivalence and needs the separately cited rank-one/line-bundle source for its proof.
items.locator: H25 introduction; Heuer, Line bundles on rigid spaces in the v-topology, Theorem 5.2

routes.title: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison, Part II: the global p-adic Simpson correspondence
routes.brief: Construct the global correspondence in Heuer's final 2025 paper on the existing analytic adic and original pro-etale carriers. Import the early local period package, coherent geometry, finite-torsion base change, perfectoid toric descent and generic Koszul/completion theory from their named owners. First extend Hodge-Tate direct images to coherent, possibly nonreduced coefficient algebras and build the relative Picard exact sequence. Construct its always representable p-divisible reduction, finite-point rigidification and Lie exponential, producing coherent canonical invertible coefficient modules without base-point choices. Independently construct canonical Higgs fields by the local small correspondence and its full endomorphism functoriality. Untwist to define an exact tensor equivalence, prove naturality for compatible lifts and exponentials, then build the global derived comparison via spectral-adic thickenings and identify its local Koszul calculation. The deliverables include unit, counit, tensor associativity, comparison maps and discriminating nilpotent, p=2 and higher-dimensional tests. Do not replace these constructions by equivalences supplied as structure fields. Full transitive source closure and G0-G8 remain acceptance conditions.
routes.reason: The parent provides period rings, linear representation functors and local comparison sheaves, not the new global categorical Simpson correspondence. This is a substantive continuation, not a second p-adic Hodge foundation. Use the early P8 cut, not the later proper comparison, and never use HWZ section 7 to prove its own input. Generic Higgs and analytic foundations remain with existing owners.
